name: Post-Construction Checklist
description: A post-construction checklist for finishing the work after the build is complete.

items.text: Remove all construction debris and waste.
Clean floors, surfaces and fixtures throughout.
Wash interior and exterior windows.
Wipe down cabinets, counters and millwork.
Clean and test plumbing fixtures and appliances.
Remove labels, protective film and packaging.
Schedule and pass all code-required final inspections.
Confirm the certificate of occupancy is obtained.
Conduct an internal quality walkthrough.
Verify accessibility and life-safety compliance.
Check fire protection and alarm systems.
Document inspection results and approvals.
items.note: Occupancy approval depends on your authority having jurisdiction; confirm requirements early.

items.text: Test and balance HVAC systems.
Verify electrical systems and emergency power.
Confirm plumbing operates without leaks.
Test controls, automation and building systems.
Verify fire and life-safety systems function.
Record commissioning results and settings.
Collect as-built drawings and updated plans.
Gather warranties for systems and materials.
Compile operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals.
Assemble inspection and test reports.
Collect product data sheets and certifications.
Organize permits and approval records.
Walk the building and create the final punch list.
Prioritize deficiencies by impact and urgency.
Assign each item to the responsible trade.
Track corrections to completion.
Re-inspect resolved items.
Document sign-off on completed deficiencies.
Prepare keys, access cards and codes.
Schedule the owner walkthrough.
Plan systems and equipment training for the owner.
Assemble the closeout and warranty package.
Confirm outstanding items and timelines.
Prepare the final account and payment documents.

faq.a: It is the period after physical construction is finished but before final handover, covering cleaning, final inspections, testing, documentation and deficiency resolution. This checklist helps builders bring the project to a truly finished state.

faq.q: What is the difference between post-construction and closeout?
faq.a: Post-construction focuses on physically finishing, cleaning, inspecting and preparing the building. Closeout is the contractual and administrative wrap-up — as-builts, warranties, final payment and lien releases. The two phases overlap and feed into each other.

faq.q: What does final construction cleaning include?
faq.a: Final cleaning removes construction dust and debris, cleans windows, fixtures, floors and surfaces, and prepares the space for occupancy. A thorough clean is essential before the owner walkthrough and any final inspections.

Reviewing and resolving deficiencies, often via a punch list, ensures the work meets the contract and quality standards before the owner accepts it. Catching issues now is far easier than after the building is occupied.

faq.q: Is this post-construction checklist available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print it for the final-stages walkthrough or download the PDF so project managers can track cleaning, inspections and handover prep from a phone or tablet.
